blocks.content:
Let us continue with the setting of the last paragraph with p,q > 0 and p + q = 1. Then the heat
kernel Kp,q(2t,x) with x ∈Z can be viewed as the probability distribution of the continuous-
time random walk on Z which steps one unit to the left (resp. right) with probability p (resp.
q = 1 −p.) Further, the time interval between steps has an exponential distribution with density
2e−2t, see [Fe66] or [Fe70, chapter 7]. In the special case when p = q = 1/2, then the function
K1/2,1/2(2t,x) = e−2tIx(2t) is the heat kernel on Z.

blocks.title: Application 1: Bessel identities
blocks.content:
Bessel functions are ubiquitous in mathematical physics, perhaps first appearing as a solution
to Bessel’s differential equations arising from the Laplace equation with cylindrical symmetry.
A classic text on Bessel functions is Watson’s book [Wa44]. The fact that the I-Bessel func-
tion is essentially a heat kernel makes many of the classical identities immediate from physical
principles. Note that we continue to view Ix(t) as a function in two variables, where the vari-
able t is continuous and where the variable x is discrete. We will now illustrate how to obtain

blocks.title: Spectral zeta function of Z
blocks.content:
The zeta function regularization method in physics started in the 1970 s with papers by
Dowker-Critchley and by Hawking. For a survey of applications to mathematical physics of
this procedure, see [V03, El12, DEK12]. The zeta function in question is defined by a integral
transform, specifically the Mellin transform, of the heat kernel. The case of the circle essen-
tially gives rise to the Riemann zeta function. It is much less standard is to take the Mellin
integral transform of e−2tIn(2t), such as

blocks.title: Potential applications to differential privacy
blocks.content:
Differential privacy is a mathematically rigorous criterion by which an algorithm that acts on
a dataset can be assessed. We refer to the article [CKS22] and references therein for an excel-
lent presentation. In practice, as described in [CKS22], one alters the output of a Z-valued
